SOURCE: "REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models", Weijia Shi, Sewon Min, Michihiro Yasunaga, Minjoon Seo, Rich James, Mike Lewis, Luke Zettlemoyer, Wen-tau Yih. Proceedings of NAACL 2024 (Volume 1: Long Papers), pages 8371–8384, June 2024. (arXiv 2301.12652.) Code: github.com/swj0419/REPLUG.
File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/02-rag-retrieval/sources/shi-2024-replug.pdf

COVERAGE: 52,327 of 52,327 chars; all 14 pages read (body pp.1–9, references pp.9–12 skimmed for origins, Appendices A–C pp.13–14 read in full). Nothing skipped. Figures 4–6 and 8 are plots whose values are only partly in the text; the numbers below are from the body text and tables, not read off the plots.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- claim: REPLUG prepends each retrieved document separately to the input of a frozen black-box LM, runs k parallel passes, and ensembles the next-token probabilities weighted by retrieval similarity; the LM is never fine-tuned.
  number: none (formula)
  setup: any LM with output probabilities; k docs from a Contriever dual encoder + FAISS index
  quote: "We prepend each document d ∈ D′ to x, pass this concatenation to the LM separately, and then ensemble output probabilities from all k passes. ... p(y | x, D′) = ∑ d∈D′ p(y | d ◦ x) · λ(d, x) ... λ(d, x) = e^{s(d,x)} / ∑ d∈D′ e^{s(d,x)}"
  where: p.4 (§3.2), chars ~15,800–16,300

- claim: The ensemble exists because context length bounds k, and it trades compute for accuracy (k LM forward passes per prediction).
  number: none
  setup: design rationale
  quote: "Because the LM context length limits the number of documents that can be prepended, we also adopt an ensemble scheme that encodes the retrieved documents in parallel with the same black-box LM, allowing us to easily trade compute for accuracy."
  where: p.1 (§1)

- claim: REPLUG LSR trains only the retriever by minimising KL between the retrieval distribution over the top-k docs and an LM-likelihood distribution (softmax over P_LM(y|d,x)); the LM is a frozen scoring function.
  number: none (formulas)
  setup: top-20 docs per query, temperature 0.1 for both softmaxes; index rebuilt every T steps
  quote: "L = 1/|B| ∑x∈B KL(QLM(d | x, y) ∥ PR(d | x)) ... When minimizing the loss, we can only update the retrieval model parameters. The LM parameters are fixed due to our black-box assumption."
  where: p.4 (§4.3)

- claim: On the Pile, REPLUG LSR cuts GPT-3 Davinci 175B bits-per-byte from 0.80 to 0.75 (6.3% relative); plain REPLUG gets 0.77 (3.8%). Curie 6.7B: 0.88 → 0.85 (3.4%) → 0.82 (6.8%).
  number: 6.3% (Davinci), 6.8% (Curie); averaged 7.7% (LSR) vs 4.7% (REPLUG) over 8 models
  setup: Pile test, BPB metric; retrieval corpus = 36M random 128-token Pile training docs; 128-token query context; top-10 docs ensembled; Contriever retriever (LSR retriever trained with Curie as supervision LM)
  quote: "Davinci 175B 0.80 0.77 3.8 0.75 6.3" (Table 1) and "REPLUG LSR results in 7.7% improvement over baselines compared to 4.7% improvement of REPLUG averaged over the 8 models."
  where: p.6 (Table 1, §6.1)

- claim: On MMLU 5-shot, Codex 175B goes from 68.3 to 71.4 (REPLUG) and 71.8 (REPLUG LSR), i.e. +4.5% and +5.1% relative; LLaMA 13B goes 55.6 → 58.8 → 59.3. Flan-PaLM 540B scores 72.2; Atlas 11B scores 47.9.
  number: 71.8 vs 68.3
  setup: 5-shot in-context learning, direct prompting; 10 docs retrieved from Wikipedia (Dec 2018) using the test question as query, ensembled; Codex = code-davinci-002
  quote: "Codex 175B 74.2 76.9 57.8 70.1 68.3 ... Codex + REPLUG 175B 76.0 79.7 58.8 72.1 71.4 / Codex + REPLUG LSR 175B 76.5 79.9 58.9 73.2 71.8" and "both the REPLUG and REPLUG LSR improve the original Codex model by 4.5% and 5.1%, respectively."
  where: p.7 (Table 2, §6.2)

- claim: Open-domain QA, 16-shot: Codex NQ EM 40.6 → 44.7 (REPLUG) → 45.5 (LSR); TriviaQA 73.6 → 76.8 → 77.3. LLaMA 13B NQ 29.0 → 36.1 → 37.2; TQA 69.6 → 73.3 → 74.1. Beats Atlas few-shot (64-shot fine-tuned, NQ 30.9 / TQA 74.5) but not full-data fine-tuned retrieval LMs (Atlas 60.4 / 79.8).
  number: 45.5 NQ, 77.3 TQA
  setup: Wikipedia corpus, top-10 docs ensembled, 16-shot in-context learning, Exact Match on filtered TriviaQA
  quote: "Codex + REPLUG LSR 45.5 - 77.3 -" (Table 3) and "REPLUG LSR significantly improves the performance of the original Codex by 12.0% on NQ and 5.0% on TQA."
  where: p.7 (Table 3, §6.3)

- claim: Gains are not from ensembling per se: ensembling random documents hurts Curie on the Pile, and gains grow monotonically with k but ~10 docs is enough.
  number: 10 docs
  setup: GPT-3 Curie, Pile BPB, random vs REPLUG vs LSR docs, varying k
  quote: "We observed that ensembling random documents leads to worse performance ... as more documents were ensembled, the performance of REPLUG and REPLUG LSR improved monotonically. However, a small number of documents (e.g., 10) was sufficient to achieve large performance gains."
  where: p.8 (§7.2), Figure 5 p.9

- claim: Among off-the-shelf retrievers, BM25 beats Contriever, DPR and BERT-base, but the LM-supervised Contriever beats BM25.
  number: none in text (Figures 6 and 8)
  setup: Wikitext-103 perplexity, GPT-2 XL 1.5B and Large 774M, Wikitext-103 train as corpus
  quote: "Among all off-the-shelf retrievers, the sparse retriever BM25 performs best. However, it still lags behind our LM supervised retriever (Contriever LSR)" and (Appendix B) "BM25 consistently outperforms Contriever but falls short when compared to LM-supervised Contriever"
  where: p.8 (§7.3), p.13 (App. B)

- claim: Gains hold across GPT-2, OPT (125M–66B) and BLOOM families and stay roughly constant with scale.
  number: OPT-125M 6.9%, OPT-66B 5.6% perplexity improvement
  setup: Wikitext-103 test perplexity; corpus = Wikitext-103 train; top-10 ensemble
  quote: "OPT-125M achieves 6.9% perplexity improvement, while OPT-66B achieves 5.6% perplexity improvement."
  where: p.8 (§7.1), Figure 4

- claim: Retrieval helps most on rare entities (qualitative).
  number: 11% continuation perplexity improvement; 15% on "Li Bai"
  setup: single Wikitext-103 example, GPT-2 1.5B, one retrieved doc
  quote: "After incorporating the retrieved document, the perplexity of the continuation improves by 11%." and "(15% for "Li Bai" and 5% for "greatest")"
  where: p.13 (Appendix A, Figure 7)

- claim: LSR training recipe.
  number: 800K queries, 36M docs, 25k steps
  setup: Pile; Contriever init; Curie supervision
  quote: "We use 800K sequences of 256 tokens each ... the first 128 tokens are used as the input context x, and the last 128 tokens are used as the ground truth continuation y. For the external corpus D, we sample 36M documents of 128 tokens from the Pile ... we retrieve the top 20 documents from the FAISS index and compute the retrieval likelihood and the LM likelihood with a temperature of 0.1. We train the retriever using the Adam optimizer ... learning rate of 2e-5, a batch size of 64, and a warmup ratio of 0.1. We re-compute the document embeddings every 3k steps and fine-tune the retriever for a total of 25k steps."
  where: p.5 (§5.2)

LIMITS
- Authors' own (§9, p.9): no interpretability ("It's unclear when the model relies on retrieved knowledge or on knowledge encoded within its own parameters"); always-on retrieval ("REPLUG always perform retrieval no matter if the external information is needed ... risk of presenting irrelevant documents ... additional computational overheads"); corpus limited to Wikipedia/Pile.
- Inference cost: k = 10 full LM forward passes per prediction (each with a document prepended); the paper frames this as "trade compute for accuracy" and never reports latency or dollar cost.
- The ensemble needs per-token output probabilities from the API; it is not applicable to chat APIs that only return sampled text. Not stated by the authors; it follows from the formula.
- No end-to-end tuning: only the retriever is trained; LM frozen. LSR supervision used Curie (6.7B) then transferred to Davinci/Codex; no ablation on supervision-LM choice.
- Retrieval likelihood marginalises only over the top-k retrieved docs, not the corpus (p.4 §4.1, acknowledged as an approximation).
- Few-shot QA still trails full-data fine-tuned retrieval LMs; authors attribute this to train/test overlap ("32.5% of test questions overlap with the training sets in NQ", p.7).
- Figures 4, 6, 8 carry numbers not reproduced in text. MMLU/QA baselines (PaLM, Flan-PaLM, Chinchilla) are copied from other papers, not re-run.
- Dated: models are GPT-3 (2020 API), Codex code-davinci-002, LLaMA 13B; Wikipedia snapshot Dec 2018. Retrieval corpus for Pile experiments is Pile training data itself (in-distribution).

BUILDS ON
- RETRO (Borgeaud et al., 2022) and Atlas (Izacard et al., 2022b): white-box retrieval LMs that update LM parameters; REPLUG contrasts with these.
- kNN-LM (Khandelwal et al., 2020; Zhong et al., 2022): needs internal representations, so not black-box.
- Contriever (Izacard et al., 2022a): the retriever used and the LSR initialisation; dual-encoder design following Qu et al. 2021 (RocketQA), Izacard and Grave 2021 (FiD), Ni et al. 2022.
- Sachan et al. (2023), "Questions are all you need to train a dense passage retriever": the inspiration for LM-likelihood supervision of the retriever.
- REALM (Guu et al., 2020): asynchronous index refresh during retriever training.
- FAISS (Johnson et al., 2019); DPR (Karpukhin et al., 2020); BM25 (Robertson et al., 2009) as baselines.
- Concurrent: Mallen et al. 2022, Si et al. 2023 (frozen retriever + GPT-3 on QA).

CODE
No code in the paper. The two formulas worth keeping verbatim (p.4):
- Ensemble: p(y | x, D′) = ∑_{d∈D′} p(y | d ◦ x) · λ(d, x), λ(d, x) = e^{s(d,x)} / ∑_{d∈D′} e^{s(d,x)}
- LSR: P_R(d|x) = e^{s(d,x)/γ} / ∑ e^{s(d,x)/γ}; Q(d|x,y) = e^{P_LM(y|d,x)/β} / ∑ e^{P_LM(y|d,x)/β}; L = (1/|B|) ∑_{x∈B} KL(Q_LM(d|x,y) ∥ P_R(d|x))
Prompt format (Table 4/5, p.14): "Knowledge: <passage>\nQuestion: <q>\nA. ... D. ...\nAnswer: <letter>" for MMLU; "Knowledge: <passage>\nQuestion: <q>\nAnswer: <a>" for QA.

FIGURES
- Figure 2, p.3: "REPLUG at inference" — retrieve, prepend each doc separately, ensemble probabilities. Best single picture of the k-parallel-passes design; explains the cost faster than the formula.
- Figure 3, p.5: "REPLUG LSR training process" — frozen LM scores docs, KL to retriever distribution. Explains LM-supervised retrieval at a glance.
- Figure 5, p.9: Curie BPB vs number of docs for random / REPLUG / LSR. Shows ensembling alone does not help and that gains saturate around 10 docs.
- Figure 6, p.9 and Figure 8, p.13: retriever comparison (BM25 > Contriever, LSR > BM25) on Wikitext-103 with GPT-2. Useful for a "BM25 is a strong baseline" point.
- Figure 1, p.1: white-box vs black-box contrast with RETRO; lower value.
- Figure 4, p.8: per-family scaling curves; values embedded as axis ticks only.

PROBLEMS
- Extraction clean; no embedded instructions found. Minor typos in source ("Baddage" for Babbage, "temerature", "Witext-103"). Figure 4 extracted as raw axis tick numbers (p.8), not data. The LLaMA reference in the bibliography is the Llama 2 paper (Touvron et al., 2023) though the body says "LLaMA 13B".
- Note for the mapping: §7.3/Appendix B (BM25 beats dense Contriever off-the-shelf; retriever tuning from LM feedback beats both) is the part most relevant to notes/11-retrieval-improvements.md; the ensemble-cost point (k forward passes, needs logprobs) is relevant to notes/01-rag-pipeline.md.
